title: KV cache allocator with thermalized slot reclamation
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: As continuous batching and long-chained chat workloads increase, our KV (key-value) cache on GPUs is experiencing non-uniform allocation patterns that lead to micro-fragmentation. This fragmentation raises peak memory by up to 12% on heavy, mixed-length tails and causes QoS variability under tight SLOs.

Goal: Design and implement an allocator and reclamation scheduler that minimizes fragmentation while preserving low-latency path for hot prefixes and cooperating with the continuous batcher to avoid unnecessary KV churn. The approach should be safe for both hosted and Dedicated environments and allow gradual rollout with telemetry-driven heuristics.

Proposal summary: Introduce a thermalized slot reclamation strategy (TSR) layered on top of the existing slab-like KV pool. Key ideas: 1) Partition pool into micro-banks sized by recent prefix length distribution; 2) Maintain per-bank age histograms and a lightweight hot-score to avoid migrating extremely hot entries; 3) Run a continuous background reclamation loop that opportunistically compacts neighboring cold slots into contiguous runs when fragmentation exceeds a threshold; 4) Coordinate with the continuous batcher to defer compaction work during high tail-latency windows and prioritize during idle bursts; 5) Provide an online telemetry signal (fragmentation_ratio, compaction_cost_tokens, reclaimed_bytes_per_min) to drive adaptive thresholds.

Design details: 1) Micro-banks: Create 4 bank classes (tiny, short, medium, long) based on token-length quantiles. Allocations route to a bank with heuristics to reduce cross-size fragmentation. 2) Thermalization: Each slot carries a 8-bit thermal counter decayed every epoch; allocation or hit increases thermal; eviction prefers low-thermal slots. 3) Compaction sweep: Background sweeper performs local defrag by copying contiguous cold slots into free spans using GPU-friendly memcpy kernels and choosing victims based on bank-local LRU+thermal score. Sweeps are bounded by a GPU time budget (configurable, default 3ms per GPU per second) to avoid interfering with inference. 4) Batcher coordination: The batcher exposes a throttle API (batcher_backpressure_score) that TSR reads; if score > 0.7, compaction is paused or lowered to sampling-only mode. 5) Soft pins: Recent KV references within last N requests (configurable) are soft-pinned preventing eviction for short windows to avoid re-population churn. 6) Fallbacks: If compaction fails to reduce fragmentation after X attempts, fall back to a conservative full-pool reclamation that compacts across banks but is gated behind maintenance windows.

Telemetry and metrics: fragmentation_ratio (free_segments / total_slots), bank_heat_map (list of 4 heat values), compaction_runtime_ms, mem_overhead_pct, eviction_repopulation_rate, requests_slowed_by_compaction. We'll add dashboards and alerts: fragmentation_ratio > 0.10 sustained for 5m triggers escalation and enables aggressive compaction in safe windows.

Testing and rollout: Stage 1 - unit tests and microbench harness on CPU-emulated pools; Stage 2 - synthetic GPU benchmarks simulating heavy mixed-length tails; Stage 3 - canary rollout on dedicated stage clusters with opt-in service flag; Stage 4 - measured gradual rollout to production with telemetry gating.

Risks and mitigations: 1) Compaction interfering with latency: mitigate with strict GPU time budgets and batcher coordination. 2) Hot-entry misclassification: mitigate with conservative thermal thresholds and soft-pins. 3) Increased memory churn due to copying: measure repopulation rate and only run compaction when net reclaimed > threshold.

Alternatives considered: 1) Fine-grained slot indirection layer (higher metadata overhead) — rejected for added pointer chasing cost. 2) Epochal stop-the-world compaction — rejected for latency impact. 3) Pure size-binning without thermalization — simpler but showed worse miss-repopulation in simulations.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Reduce 95th percentile GPU memory overhead by >= 6% on representative production traces. 2) Keep P99 per-request latency regressions < 1% during canary. 3) No increase in error rates or model output degradation.

Deliverables: design doc link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1kv-thermalization-design (internal), PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/xxxxx, perf dashboards, runbook for toggling TSR flags.
